*Generated by `eval/figs_results_walkthrough.py` at commit `5c2f854`. This script only COMPOSES pages: it places existing, cross-checked images (thesis figures, summary charts, the all-flights plots of `eval/figs_walkthrough_flights.py` and the composite figures of `eval/figs_walkthrough_extra.py`, whose own checks are in `flights/index_flights.md` and `extra/index_extra.md`); nothing is re-plotted, recomputed or re-run here. All provenance is here; the pages carry none.*

**Restructure (user request 2026-10-29; decisions D61 onward in `docs/thesis/tier1/decisions_log.md`):** redundant plots removed; a setup section shows the corridor and the tag room, and where the drone flew in each, once; every world is pictured once; the Metric / Pass rule / Result block of each summary page is printed exactly once in the PDF (asserted: 57/57 lines once); Experiment 4 (live and hindsight) and Experiment 5 (hold and drift) are merged figures with one y-scale each; Extension E4 is a redesigned two-panel figure (compute time | live error); the E3 verdict table, the E3 maps and the E4 change plot are in an appendix. No em-dash in any page text (asserted).

## Page 01 (plot, PDF page 7): Experiment 1A: position error with standard sensors, checkerboard floor (1 of 2)

- **File:** `walkthrough/wt_01_1A_fig42.png`
- **Plot:** `docs/thesis/figures_thesis/R3_trajectory_overlay.png` (sha256 `4f71bf4950b3b37e8f4cd7b97ac9823f68900790b42089e1aed2ea119eda48d5`), crop box (x0, y0, x1, y1) px: (507, 104, 2014, 900); shown 4.25 in tall, scale 1.07

| line | kind | source | check | text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | VERBATIM | summary page 01, title + page counter | equal | Experiment 1A: position error with standard sensors, checkerboard floor (1 of 2) |
| What this tests | VERBATIM | summary page 01, what | equal | How accurately three position estimators track a drone along a long indoor corridor with no GPS, using only motion sensors, a downward camera and a height sensor. |
| About this plot | NEW | new (this script) | numbers found | FITTED (aligned): Figure 4.2 (a) of the thesis: one example flight (flight 3, chosen beforehand as the median flight), all three estimators on one plot, cruise only. The whole estimated path is slid and turned as one rigid piece, about the vertical only, to lie as close as possible to the true path; it cannot bend or stretch it. So the error left measures how well the estimator tracked the shape of the flight, not which way it happened to start pointing. This makes the error smaller than the raw drift (see the not-fitted page). This fit gives the same average error (ATE) as the standard alignment used for the score. |
| This plot shows | NEW | new (this script) | numbers found | the fitted estimated paths; the experiment's score below is the fitted average error (ATE) between these and the true paths. |
| Metric | MODIFIED | summary page 01, metric | numbers found | average position error over the straight cruise (after a best-fit alignment), median of 9 flights per estimator, metres.; ORIGINAL: average position error over the straight cruise (after a best-fit alignment), median of 9 flights per estimator, metres (the vertical lines show the range over the flights). |
| Pass rule | VERBATIM | summary page 01, rule | equal | EKF3 and the FGO were ranked only if one was lower on at least 6 of 7 further flights AND the 95% confidence interval of the difference excluded zero (the same rule either way); no ranking rule was registered for the UKF. |
| Result | VERBATIM | summary page 01, result | equal | NOT MET: on the further flights EKF3 was lower on 5 of 7 and the interval (−0.989 to +0.947 m) includes zero, so no estimator is ranked above another. |

The whole estimated path is slid and turned as one rigid piece, about the vertical only, to lie as close as possible to the true path; it cannot bend or stretch it. So the error left measures how well the estimator tracked the shape of the flight, not which way it happened to start pointing. This makes the error smaller than the raw drift (see the not-fitted page). This fit gives the same average error (ATE) as the standard alignment used for the score. |
| This plot shows | NEW | new (this script) | numbers found | the fitted estimated paths; the experiment's score below is the fitted average error (ATE) between these and the true paths. |

## Removed in the 2026-10-29 restructure (user request), and why

- **1A:** fitted paths of all flights, fitted error against time (its U-shape comes from the alignment), raw paths from take-off (the raw error against time covers the drift). Kept: Figure 4.2 (a) and the raw error against time.
- **1B:** five-panel fitted paths, fitted error against time and raw error against time (with and without the heading); the with-heading raw error is stated in text on the five-panel raw paths page (checked in `flights/index_flights.md`).
- **1C:** both 'true sideways position' plots; the with-heading largest sideways distance is one sentence on the with-heading page.
- **'Where the drone really flew'** pages of 1B, 1C (other than the kept paths plot), 2, 3, 4, 5 and 5S: the corridor path and the 6 m square are shown once, in the setup section. The outdoor-indoor route and the hold routes are no longer drawn anywhere.
- **Repeated world pages:** the tag room once (setup), the wall-tag room once (Experiment 5, also for 5S), the forward-camera corridors once (1B, also for the ablation).
- **Standalone E4 compute-time page:** its plot is the left panel of the new E4 figure.
- **Moved to the appendix:** the E3 verdict table, the E3 tag maps (optional), the E4 change-from-0.25 s plot.
